text:
alex: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak last night, my A10 runs show max-tokens-per-batch effectively lower by ~25% for long-context workloads. Repro steps below.
maria: ugh, that sounds like the kernel fallthrough we feared. Can you paste the perf numbers?
alex: yes — ran bench/continuous_batch.sh against model-repro:v3 with seq=2048 and mixed batch shapes. Command:
```
./bench/continuous_batch.sh --model model-repro:v3 --device a10 --seq 2048 --duration 60
```
Output (summary):
```
mean_tokens_per_batch: 1792
p50_latency_ms: 42
throughput_tok_s: 54000
kernel_selected: aten_fused_attn (fallback path triggered 68% of time)
kv_cache_frag_ratio: 0.23
```
alex: before the selector change we were at mean_tokens_per_batch ~2400 and throughput ~72k tok/s for same config.
kevin: do we know which kernel selector rule caused the fallback? maybe the seq/shape heuristic now prefers a non-optimized path for certain packing ratios.
sam: I profiled a single step with nvprof and saw more small kernels scheduled, plus a bunch of memcpy calls on A10. looks like packing introduces fragmentation and selector picks safer kernel.
maria: can you share the nvprof snippet? even a few lines helps.
sam: pasted trimmed snippet below:
```
MemcpyHtoD: 12.3ms  calls=4
multi_head_attn_fused_kernel_v1: 3.1ms
multi_head_attn_fallback: 9.8ms
small_reduce_kernel: 2.2ms  calls=18
```
maria: fallback time explains latency jump. Also note kv_cache_frag_ratio 0.23 — that will lower effective batch tokens because we can't pack as densely.
jen: Is this specific to A10? Any sign on T4/L4/A100/H100?
alex: quick smoke: T4 looks less affected (only ~8% drop) but H100/A100 saw variable behavior — H100 had the selector pick the optimized kernel more often, so no regression there.
kevin: that matches kernel table — the new rule checks available shared memory and falls back on A10 when packing causes higher per-slice shared mem usage. A100/H100 have more headroom so they stay on fast kernel.
maria: proposed interim mitigations:
- revert the selector rule for devices with < 40MB shared memory (A10/T4/L4) OR
- add packing-aware selector: estimate kv_frag and prefer kernel with better packing tolerance OR
- tune max_tokens_per_batch down on A10 only to avoid triggering fallback
Which is lowest friction?
alex: revert rule is easiest but risky (we added it for correctness on some edge cases). Tuning per-device max_tokens seems fine short-term.
sam: we should also add an experiment variant that forces the old kernel to verify perf diff, then run canary for 24h.
jen: can we get a quick numbers table from alex for A10 with three configs: baseline (pre-selector), post-selector, and post-selector + max_tokens cap=2000?
alex: ran that overnight. results (A10, seq2048):
```
baseline_pre: mean_tokens_per_batch=2420 throughput=72.1k tok/s p50=36ms
post_selector: mean_tokens_per_batch=1792 throughput=54.0k tok/s p50=42ms
cap_2000: mean_tokens_per_batch=2000 throughput=61.2k tok/s p50=39ms
```
kevin: cap_2000 recovers a fair bit. suggests packing triggers selector threshold — lowering target keeps shapes that hit optimized kernel.
maria: OK action items:
- alex: open PR that adds device-specific max_tokens softcap (A10=2000, T4=1800, L4=1900) + telemetry to log kernel choice and kv_frag ratio per batch (owner alex) — due EOD PT.
- sam: run forced-kernel experiment on staging (force optimized kernel on A10) and capture regressions (owner sam) — start now, report in 6h.
- kevin: audit selector rule that checked shared mem threshold and add simulated packing test so it doesn't misfire (owner kevin) — unblock by tomorrow.
- jen: coordinate canary config with infra (owner jen).
ci-bot: perf-regression alert: A10 throughput drop detected on model-repro:v3 at 2025-10-12T03:12:00Z (investigating tags: kernel-selector)
maria: thanks. keep notes short in the PR. Important: include small reproducible script, and add a heatmap of kv_frag vs tokens_per_batch so we can tune the cap automatically later.
alex: will do. attaching quick patch notes in the PR comment when ready.
kevin: FYI, I'll add a unit test for the selector that simulates packing with random shapes so we don't regress again.
sam: started forced-kernel run — first 30m looks promising, will post logs.
jen: ping me once sam has the logs, I'll schedule canary rollout.
alex: thanks all. I'll file the PR and include the bench output above.
maria: nice triage. small follow-up: let's add a metric to console dashboards for 'kernel_fallback_rate' by device so product teams can see impact.
kevin: agreed, will add to roadmap for Optimize.
alex: incremental update: PR #4523 opened with softcap and telemetry, link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4523 :thumbsup:
sam: forced-kernel experiment logs: 1771112500-forced-a10-kernel.log (uploaded) — early numbers show throughput back to baseline within noise.
maria: perfect. close loop once canary is green, then we decide whether to revert selector or keep cap + longer-term selector fix.
